Alex: Heads up — after the merge that landed around 10:30 (commit abc1234) we're seeing a p95 decode increase ~20% on short-sequence real-traffic traces. CI perf alert: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/9843 showed +18% p95 for decode-path. Reproducer attached (shortseq workload).

Jamie: Can you paste the profiler output / flame?

Alex: quick snippet from perf flame and logs:
```
time in decode_dispatch: +21%
  attention_kernel_dispatch: +15%  <-- more calls
  kernel_selector: choose=fallback_matmul_small (was fused_attn before)
  batcher: avg_batch_size_tokens=8 (prev 24)
```
Full flame at /tmp/flame-4567.svg.

Priya: Interesting — batcher avg_tokens dropping from 24->8 would explain more kernel launches and missing fused path. Any recent change to batching heuristics or the shortseq threshold? @Taylor did you touch the batcher thresholds in the PR that landed? :eyes:

Taylor: I touched the batching decision logic in PR #8721 but only for the long tail — I added an early-exit when queue latency > 12ms to avoid head-of-line stalls. I didn't intentionally change token thresholds. I'll re-check.

ci-bot: PERF ALERT: build 9843 -> decode_p95 delta +18% (regression detected against baseline 9810). Canary hold flagged.

Jamie: Could be the early-exit interacting with warmup behavior: when queue latency is high we now flush smaller micro-batches more eagerly which could drop us out of `fused_attn` path because the kernel_selector prefers larger token counts for that path. If fused_attn has a minimum total-token threshold, micro-batches will route elsewhere.

Alex: I dumped kernel_selector decisions from a live canary trace (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T10:22:01Z] seq_len=16 batch_tokens=8 -> fallback_matmul_small
[2026-03-17T10:22:01Z] seq_len=16 batch_tokens=24 -> fused_attn
```
So same input sometimes hits different kernels depending on observed batch_tokens.

Priya: Run a quick experiment: temporarily bump the batcher min-accum_tokens back to previous value (24) or disable the early flush and re-run the shortseq perf test. If perf goes back to baseline that's our regression. Can someone run?

Taylor: I'll run a quick patch on canary config to disable the new early-exit and re-run the synthetic shortseq perf suite. ETA 30m.

Alex: I started a git-bisect plan to narrow commits between abc1000..abc1300 (includes #8721). Plan: bisect with microbench harness that reproduces decode p95. Command: `./tools/bisect_perf --metric decode_p95 --threshold +10% --range abc1000..abc1300`. Will post results.

Jamie: Also add a tiny unit/regression test: ensure kernel_selector picks `fused_attn` for batch_tokens >= 20 for our typical shortseq model. Add to perf-suite so CI catches this next time.

Taylor: Quick canary run done — disabling early-exit shaved p95 back ~19% to within noise. Re-enabled fuse route in logs. Looks like the early flush is the trigger for microbatching.

Priya: Ok that's enough signal to treat this as a rollout blocker. Options: revert PR #8721, or adjust threshold to be latency-aware but maintain min-accum_tokens. Prefer a targeted fix: make early-exit only trigger if predicted fused_attn_loss == false (i.e., don't flush if it would drop us out of fused path).

Alex: Agreed. I'll update the PR with a guard and add an integration test. Also queued a rollback candidate in case we need immediate mitigation: revert abc1234 -> will patch release if needed.

ci-bot: CANARY HOLD: canary release paused due to perf regression.

Taylor: filing a follow-up issue with perf numbers, test plan, and the proposed guard: https://issues.redwood/INF-3721. I'll also run the full traffic replay overnight after the change.

Alex: Thanks all — plan: (1) temp revert if bisect pins it to #8721, (2) implement guard + regression test, (3) re-run canary and traffic replay. I'll update thread with bisect outcome (running now). :thumbsup:
